correctness.rationale: The Jacobson radical contains exactly strictly level-increasing matrix blocks (diagonal quotient is a product of fields), hence J^h=0. A product of h-1 radical factors must use every adjacent level exactly once; x^(h-1) has only B_1...B_(h-1) in the first-to-last block, so q^(M-D) other parameters are free. If a partial product has rank r, multiplication by an independent uniform n_i x n_(i+1) matrix is equivalent to a uniform r x n_(i+1) matrix with q^((n_i-r)n_(i+1)) lifts. Gaussian-binomial image-and-surjection counting proves the displayed rank recurrence, all q prime powers and widths. A rank-2/rank-1 absorbing Markov chain yields p2=a^(h-1), p1=(q+1)/q(c^(h-1)-a^(h-1)), and p0 by subtraction. For q=2, three layers of width two, I independently enumerated 256 consecutive-block pairs with product rank populations (58,162,36); multiplying by 16 free remote blocks yields the predicted full radical counts (928,2592,576). I inspected the original GF(4) arithmetic and saved count logs, which are corroboration only.
